slides.title: A key for your house
slides.text: Your house key opens your front door, and only your front door. Pim says a good key is kept safe, never lent out, and never left lying around.
slides.alt: Lock It, safe habit or risky habit: a habit card waits to be sorted, and Pim asks how you keep a key.

focus.cue: If one key opens every door, losing it opens them all
Safe or risky: changing the key when a site leaks it

slides.title: A key for your mailbox
slides.text: In Netville, your mailbox has a key too, and that key is a passphrase. It locks your letters away so only the right person can open them.
slides.alt: Lock It: build a mailbox key for Pim from four word tiles, and watch the meter.

focus.cue: Build a mailbox key for Pim from four word tiles

slides.title: Build a passphrase
slides.text: Pick four random words that do not belong together. Picture them in one funny scene, like a giraffe riding a bicycle up a volcano in the thunder.
slides.alt: A mailbox key built from four word tiles: volcano, giraffe, bicycle, thunder. A guessing computer would need hundreds of years.

focus.cue: Picked words land in your passphrase
The meter: guessing would take hundreds of years

slides.title: Who may know it?
slides.text: Only you and a trusted adult may know your passphrase. Never share it with your best friend, even if they promise to keep it secret.
slides.alt: Lock It, who may know your key: a card waits for its tray, Okay to tell or Keep it to yourself.

focus.cue: Only the trusted adults who look after your account may know
A trusted adult at home: okay to tell

words.means: a secret key made of several random words
only for you and the trusted adults who look after you
something only you and a trusted adult should know
an adult you trust who helps keep you safe, like a parent or teacher

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Packet Post at Lock It and finish all 6 levels. In the game your passphrase is called your mailbox key. You only tap tiles, so nothing real gets shared.
slides.alt: Three random words in the passphrase so far. The meter says a computer would need about a hundred years.

focus.cue: Open Lock It and build mailbox keys from word tiles
